## Setup

```{r}
#| echo: false
options(conflicts.policy = "depends.ok")
library(tidyverse)
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/main/format_path.R")
source(here::here("scripts", "functions_llmpanel.R"))

path_processed <- format_path("llmpanel/data_processed")
raw_panel <- read_csv(here::here(path_processed, "panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

pref_cols <- c("pref_legitimizing", "pref_norms", "pref_value_affirmation",
               "pref_self_efficacy", "pref_acknowledging")

# Tier colors from the preference survey (red = Norms, amber = Acknowledging,
# green = Legitimizing, Self efficacy, Value affirmation)
tier_colors <- c(norms = "#E24B4A", acknowledging = "#BA7517", legitimizing = "#639922",
                 self_efficacy = "#639922", value_affirmation = "#639922")

# Wide format with each respondent's highest- and lowest-preferred tone(s) and a
# straightliner flag
panel <- format_eda(raw_panel) |> add_pref_extremes(pref_cols)

# Angled x-axis labels so tone names are not cut off
angled_x_labels <- theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
                         plot.margin = margin(5.5, 5.5, 5.5, 20))

# Long format (one row per message rating) and each respondent's mean rating per tone
panel_long <- format_eda(raw_panel, long = TRUE)
rating_by_tone <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, tone))
```

Groups are defined by each respondent's preference scores: the highest tier is the tone(s)
tied for the highest score, and the lowest tier the tone(s) tied for the lowest. Respondents
who gave the same score to every tone (straightliners) are excluded from the grouped plots.

# Preferences and ratings are broadly aligned

```{r}
# Faceted plot showing bar charts for the mean tone preferences next to
# mean message ratings by tone
pref_vs_rating <- bind_rows(
  panel |>
    select(all_of(pref_cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "tone", names_prefix = "pref_", values_to = "value") |>
    summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
              se = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(value))),
              .by = tone) |>
    mutate(measure = "Mean preference (preferences survey)"),
  rating_by_tone |>
    summarise(mean = mean(rating), se = sd(rating) / sqrt(n()), .by = tone) |>
    mutate(measure = "Mean message rating")) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Mean preference (preferences survey)",
                                              "Mean message rating")))

# Same tone order in both panels (lowest to highest mean message rating)
tone_by_rating <- pref_vs_rating |>
  filter(measure == "Mean message rating") |>
  arrange(mean) |>
  pull(tone)

pref_vs_rating |>
  mutate(tone = factor(tone, levels = tone_by_rating)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tone, y = mean, fill = tone)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se), width = 0.25) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 1.5, label = round(mean, 2)), color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~measure) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tier_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_to_sentence(str_replace(x, "_", " "))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(x = "Tone", y = "Mean (1-7)") +
  angled_x_labels
```

# Self-Efficacy and Value Affirmation are rated highly regardless of preference

```{r}
# Box plots showing the distribution of message ratings across tones, for
# individuals for whom self efficacy is in their lowest tier of preferences
# (left) vs. their highest tier of preferences (right)
plot_ratings_by_tier("self_efficacy", panel, rating_by_tone, tier_colors)
```

```{r}
# Same plot as above for individuals with value affirmation in their lowest tier
# (left) vs. their highest tier (right)
plot_ratings_by_tier("value_affirmation", panel, rating_by_tone, tier_colors)
```

# Norms is rated highly only among those with a strong preference

```{r}
# Faceted categorical box plots:
# Top: Box plot with mean message ratings across all tones
# Bottom: Box plot for individuals with norms in the highest tier of preferences
plot_ratings_by_groups(
  list("All respondents" = unique(rating_by_tone$subid),
       "Norms in highest preference tier" = pref_group_ids(panel, "norms", "top")),
  rating_by_tone, tier_colors)
```

```{r}
# Norms in the lowest tier of preferences (left) vs. the highest tier (right)
plot_ratings_by_tier("norms", panel, rating_by_tone, tier_colors)
```

# Legitimizing is rated moderately, regardless of preference

```{r}
# Faceted categorical box plots:
# Top: Individuals for whom legitimizing is in the lowest tier of preferences

plot_ratings_by_tier("legitimizing", panel, rating_by_tone, tier_colors)
```

# Acknowledging is rated poorly, regardless of preference

```{r}

```

# Within-person check: do people rate a tone higher when they prefer it more?

Moved from `followup_analyses.qmd` (Section 5; now in `scripts/archive/`). Feeds Table 10 of the capstone write-up.

The preference report compares groups (tone in highest vs. lowest tier), which
mixes in people who rate everything high. This model asks the within-person
question directly: when a respondent prefers a tone more than their own
average, do they rate messages in that tone higher? The slope is estimated
separately for each tone.

-   `pref_dev`: the respondent's preference for the message's tone minus their
    mean preference across the five tones.
-   `pref_mean`: their mean preference (a general tendency to agree).

```{r}
#| label: Within-Person Preference Model
# Each respondent's preference score for each tone (long format)
pref_by_tone <- panel_long |>
  distinct(subid, across(all_of(pref_cols))) |>
  pivot_longer(-subid, names_to = "tone", names_prefix = "pref_", values_to = "pref")

pref_model_data <- panel_long |>
  left_join(pref_by_tone |> rename(pref_own = pref), by = c("subid", "tone")) |>
  mutate(pref_mean = mean(pref_own, na.rm = TRUE), .by = subid) |>
  mutate(pref_dev = pref_own - pref_mean,
         subid = factor(subid),
         tone = factor(tone, levels = tone_levels),
         style = factor(style),
         context = factor(context)) |>
  drop_na(rating_num, pref_dev)

m_pref <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone * pref_dev + pref_mean + style + context +
    (1 | subid) + (1 | subid:tone),
  data = pref_model_data, REML = FALSE)

# Does the preference slope differ by tone?
m_pref_common <- update(m_pref, . ~ . - tone:pref_dev)
anova(m_pref_common, m_pref)

# Slope of rating on own preference, per tone (points of rating per point of preference)
pref_slopes <- emmeans::emtrends(m_pref, ~ tone, var = "pref_dev",
                                 lmer.df = "asymptotic")
pref_slopes
pairs(pref_slopes, adjust = "holm")
```

```{r}
#| label: Preference Slope Plot
# Forest plot of the slope for each tone: change in message rating per 1-point higher
# preference for that tone, with 95% intervals
as_tibble(pref_slopes) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pref_dev.trend, y = fct_reorder(tone, pref_dev.trend))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = asymp.LCL, xmax = asymp.UCL)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_to_sentence(str_replace(x, "_", " "))) +
  labs(x = "Change in message rating per 1-point higher preference for that tone",
       y = NULL)
```

Expectation from the preference report: the largest slope for norms, and
slopes near zero for self efficacy and acknowledging.
